argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only in its caveated form. Aggregate readiness clears the launch threshold by 2.0 percentage points and the launch rehearsal shows no severity-one incidents, which supports overall launch readiness. But the same admissible record also shows a current named-use-case weakness in pharmacy prior authorization, concentrated in coverage criteria summarization, and the proposed runbook remains draft with TBD owner and alert threshold. Under that record, the strongest supportable certification position is not clean certification; it is certification with explicit disclosure of the pharmacy limitation and the current mitigation status.
claims_about_business_cost: No admissible evidence is needed to see that escalation beyond a caveated compliance treatment is unnecessary on this record. The record already supports a bounded path: preserve certification, preserve disclosure of the unresolved pharmacy limitation, and avoid treating the draft runbook as if it were an approved mitigation. That addresses the policy gap without forcing a broader challenge to launch readiness.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy text is narrower than a general launch-readiness standard. Certification without material caveats requires either current evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence does not establish either predicate. The policy therefore does not support caveat-free certification. It does support certification if the unresolved limitation is disclosed, because the release policy separately requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
concessions: The current record does not support any claim of clean certification without material caveats.
The draft runbook does not satisfy the policy predicate for an approved mitigation because the accountable owner and alert threshold are still TBD, and no approved risk acceptance is in evidence.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not, by themselves, eliminate the named pharmacy prior-authorization weakness.
